state_build.title: Building a State, 1897–1948
state_build.sub: How a political program became a state in 51 years — the institutions, the patrons, and the votes, in order.

steps.x: Herzl's First Zionist Congress in Basel founds the World Zionist Organization with a goal: a publicly secured home in Palestine.
The movement builds a bank and the Jewish National Fund, which buys land held permanently for Jews.
Britain's Balfour Declaration pledges support for a "national home" — while promising not to prejudice the rights of the Arab majority.
The League of Nations Mandate writes Balfour into international law and recognizes a "Jewish agency" to cooperate with the administration.
The Jewish Agency's US allies build a domestic political machine aimed at Congress, the parties, and the White House.
UNSCOP recommends partition; the US lobbies wavering states; Resolution 181 passes 33–13.
Israel declares independence; about 750,000 Palestinians are displaced. Land, banking, diplomacy, and votes all converge.

aipac_machine.title: The AIPAC Machine
aipac_machine.sub: How money, trips, and primaries connect — and loop back.

steps.x: Individual donors fund two vehicles: a traditional PAC and a super PAC with no spending limit.
AIPAC's PAC gives directly to members of both parties — the top-25 lists are in the Congress chapter.
AIPAC's affiliated charity, AIEF, sends members of Congress to Israel — the Western Wall photo is part of the itinerary.
The super PAC spends to unseat critics — over $15 million against Bowman and Bush in 2024.
Votes are scored; deviations draw primary money. The machine is contestable — see the 2026 vote — but its incentives are documented.

aid_cycle.title: The Aid Cycle
aid_cycle.sub: Where a US military-aid dollar goes — and why it keeps renewing.

steps.x: Congress funds the 10-year MOU — $3.8B a year, the largest US military-aid pledge in history.
Foreign Military Financing routes it through the State Department and Pentagon.
Under buy-American terms, the money pays US contractors — 80%+ of post-October 7 aid went to five firms.
Weapons go to Israel's military; Israel's own exports hit a record $14.8B in 2024.
Talks on the next MOU began in 2026. Since 1951 the aid has never been "freed" — it renews.

phone_profile.title: Phone to Profile
phone_profile.sub: How data about anyone becomes an enforcement file — without a warrant.

steps.x: Apps and ad code log your location; fake cell towers capture every phone in range.
Data brokers sell location histories; ICE's own legal memo says buying them requires no warrant.
Cellebrite, an Israeli firm, unlocks seized phones for US agencies.
Palantir combines purchased data with government records — including tax data newly shared with ICE.
The profile drives enforcement. Built for immigrants; the same system scales to anyone.

ice_israel.title: The ICE–Israel Pipeline
ice_israel.sub: Who supplies US immigration enforcement — and each supplier's distance from the State of Israel.

steps.x: Stephen Miller sets the target: 3,000 arrests a day.
ICE buys software, spyware, phone-cracking tools, towers, and detention beds.
Elbit and Cellebrite are Israeli; Paragon is Israeli-founded; Palantir partners with Israel's Defense Ministry.
Miller's own disclosure lists up to $250,000 in Palantir stock — the vendor that executes the policy.

nypd_israel.title: NYPD ↔ Israel
nypd_israel.sub: A city police force with a post inside Israel's national police — lawful, privately funded, outside the settlements.

steps.x: In 2002 the NYPD created an International Liaison Program; a detective has been posted at Israel National Police HQ ever since.
A private foundation helps pay for it — so the City Council doesn't appropriate it.
The Demographics Unit mapped Muslim communities for years — and produced no terrorism leads, per the NYPD's own testimony.
US police officials travel to Israel on ADL- and JINSA-sponsored trips.
Settlements test conduct, the foundation avoids the council, and no one has standing to sue.

fed_1913.title: The Fed, 1913 — Structure vs. Myth
fed_1913.sub: What the Federal Reserve actually is — and why the "Zionist Fed" claim fails the record.

steps.x: The US suffered a banking panic roughly every 15 years; in 1907 the backstop was one banker's fortune.
Congress passed the Federal Reserve Act in 1913: a public, Senate-confirmed Board and 12 regional banks owned by member banks.
Paul Warburg helped design it — documented.
His brother Felix and father-in-law Jacob Schiff were prominent non- and anti-Zionists; the "Zionist Fed" link has no primary source and traces to a 1950s conspiracy writer.

net_kushner.title: Jared Kushner — Network
net_kushner.sub: Documented ties, and each node's distance from the State of Israel.

steps.x: Jared Kushner: real-estate heir, adviser, envoy, investor.
The family foundation, with Jared a director, gave to settlement groups and to Friends of the IDF, on whose board he sat.
He brokered the Abraham Accords and presented the Gaza masterplan; Netanyahu is a longtime family friend.
Affinity holds $2B from Saudi Arabia; Israeli insurers were partners in the family company.

net_miller.title: Stephen Miller — Network
net_miller.sub: Documented ties, and each node's distance from the State of Israel.

steps.x: Sessions aide, Breitbart's source, then the White House.
He sets ICE's quota and founded America First Legal between terms.
His stock is in Palantir, which partners with Israel's Defense Ministry and runs ICE's systems.

net_shillman.title: The Shillman / TPUSA Hub
net_shillman.sub: One donor behind several pro-Israel voices for young conservatives — and the paths to Israel.

edges.l: Israeli government asks it to build projects

steps.x: Robert Shillman funds TPUSA, the Horowitz fellowships that launched Ben Shapiro, and PragerU.
He sits on the board of Friends of the IDF; TPUSA also took $700,000 from the IFCJ.
Charlie Kirk spoke at Im Tirtzu's 2019 Jerusalem event; in 2025 Shillman withdrew a $2M pledge as Kirk platformed Israel critics.

net_ellison.title: Larry Ellison — Network
net_ellison.sub: Platforms, media, and documented paths to the State of Israel.

steps.x: Larry Ellison — Oracle co-founder.
The largest gift in Friends of the IDF's history; Netanyahu hosted on his island.
Oracle oversees TikTok's US algorithm; the family owns CBS. Netanyahu called TikTok "the most important purchase." No evidence yet shows the algorithm tilted.

net_rubio.title: Marco Rubio — Network
net_rubio.sub: Documented ties, and each node's distance from the State of Israel.

steps.x: Rubio: Secretary of State, acting national security adviser, and more — appointed by the 2016 rival he called a "con artist."
About $1.01 million from pro-Israel PACs and donors over his career.
Loomer says she called him; the next day State halted visas for injured Gazan children.
State sanctions those who investigate Israel and waives Congress's review to rush arms to it.

net_epstein.title: Jeffrey Epstein — Network
net_epstein.sub: The documented money and ties — and each node's distance from the State of Israel. Intelligence claims are marked where the record stops.

steps.x: Epstein had no family fortune. Wexner gave him power of attorney; Leon Black paid him about $170 million; he put $40 million into Thiel's fund.
Ghislaine Maxwell — the one conviction — is the daughter of Robert Maxwell, given an Israeli state funeral in 1991.
Former Israeli PM Ehud Barak did business with Epstein after his conviction; Epstein's money reached Carbyne, the company Barak chaired.
A claim that Epstein "belonged to intelligence" is second-hand and was never confirmed. No agency direction is documented.

net_thiel.title: Peter Thiel — Network
net_thiel.sub: Palantir, the funds, the politicians — and each node's distance from the State of Israel.

steps.x: Thiel co-founded Palantir, which partners with Israel's Defense Ministry and runs ICE's systems. No Israeli investor appears in its ownership — a checked finding.
Valar took $40 million of Epstein's money; Founders Fund led a $15M round into Carbyne, chaired by Ehud Barak.
Thiel invested in Curtis Yarvin's startup and backed J.D. Vance's rise to the Senate and vice presidency.

net_adelson.title: The Adelsons — Network
net_adelson.sub: Over $550 million in political giving, a newspaper in Israel, and the policies they pressed for.

steps.x: About $557 million in lifetime political giving — $90 million of one pro-Trump super PAC's $105 million in 2020, over $100 million in 2024.
They pressed for the embassy move and Golan recognition; both happened in Trump's first term. Miriam received the Medal of Freedom.
Miriam publishes Israel Hayom, Israel's most-read paper; the family owns the Las Vegas Review-Journal.
Reports said support was conditioned on backing West Bank annexation; her spokesperson rejected them. Giving and outcomes are documented; purchase is not.

christian_zionism.title: Christian Zionism — From a Footnote to a Foreign Policy
christian_zionism.sub: How an annotated Bible became a political constituency.

steps.x: Cyrus Scofield's annotated Bible framed a Jewish state as prophecy — a view largely absent from Protestant tradition before it.
CUFI (2006, 10M+ members) mobilizes voters; the IFCJ channels evangelical giving to Israel.
Netanyahu speaks at CUFI summits; the IFCJ paid TPUSA $700,000 for campus Israel programming.
Evangelical pressure, documented in White House statements, helped drive the 2018 embassy move — a constituency that lobbies independently of AIPAC.

money_1948.title: Follow the Money, 1897–1948
money_1948.sub: From blue-box coins to Czech fighters — every stream documented in the Road to 1948, in order.

steps.t: 1899–1901 · A bank and a land fund
steps.x: Small donors buy £1 shares in the movement's own bank and drop coins in the blue box for the land fund.
The Jaffa bank lends to settlers; the land fund buys and never resells — 936,000 dunams by 1947.
Keren Hayesod and US tours build a donor base; in 1929 non-Zionist American money joins the Jewish Agency.
The Haavara agreement turns German Jewish assets into exports to Palestine; ~60,000 people resettle.
A secret donor network buys arms; Golda's tour raises ~$50M, much of it spent on Czechoslovak weapons.

steps.t: 1948 · The state, and one policy purchase
steps.x: The state is declared and recognized. One documented money-for-policy moment: $100,000 for a broke campaign as Truman backs off pressure.

info_war.title: The Information War, 1941–1948
info_war.sub: Two machines — one rival, one mainstream — moving American opinion and Congress.

steps.x: The Irgun's Bergson group runs aggressive public campaigns; the mainstream AZEC builds a disciplined lobby.
Full-page ads and "We Will Never Die" reach tens of thousands; AZEC's local committees flood Washington with letters.
Committees of prominent Christians — organized from the Zionist office — present support as independent.
Rescue pressure precedes the War Refugee Board; Palestine enters both party platforms for the first time.

steps.t: 1946–47 · To the White House and the UN
steps.x: Access through aide David Niles; the 1946 Yom Kippur statement; US pressure for the partition vote.

warnings_1947.title: Warned, Then Overruled — 1946–1948
warnings_1947.sub: Every documented official warning against partition, and the political advice that prevailed.

nodes.s: Apr 1946 · neither Jewish nor Arab state

steps.x: The Anglo-American Committee recommends a state that is neither Jewish nor Arab; Washington keeps only the 100,000 admissions.
State's Near East chief, the Joint Chiefs, and the Defense Secretary warn in writing that partition will harm US interests.

steps.t: 28 Nov 1947 · The CIA's first big estimate
steps.x: ORE-55 predicts war if partition passes and warns US interests will be endangered.

steps.t: The other side of the scale
steps.x: Clifford and Niles argue the domestic political case; a personal channel through Eddie Jacobson reaches Weizmann.
The US backs partition and recognizes Israel eleven minutes after independence.

net_bengvir.title: Itamar Ben-Gvir — Network
net_bengvir.sub: Documented ties, and each node's distance from the State of Israel.

steps.x: Youth coordinator in Kach — the Kahanist movement banned in Israel and designated a terrorist group after 1994.
Co-founds Otzma Yehudit (2012); shares its headquarters with Lehava; builds a 2024–26 alliance with Chabad networks.
A 2021 joint-list deal brokered by Netanyahu seats him; in December 2022 he takes the National Security Ministry — police and prisons.
In June 2025 five US allies impose travel bans and sanctions; the US does not.
He campaigns to become defense minister ahead of the October 27 election.

me_layers.title: How the Middle East Evolved, 1516–1979
me_layers.sub: The layers that stacked up — empire, democracy, oil, borders, kings, revolts, 1948, coups, revolution.

steps.x: Four centuries of Ottoman rule with no borders between today's states.
Iran wins a parliament, loses it to Russian and British pressure; oil makes the region a prize.
Britain and France draw the borders and pick the kings; revolts follow.
Israel's founding, ~700,000 Palestinian refugees, the departure of Jewish communities from Arab lands, and discredited regimes.

steps.t: 1949–1958 · Coups, and Iran's second democracy ended
steps.x: Syria, Egypt, Suez, Iraq — and the CIA–MI6 coup against Mosaddegh.
Occupation, the oil weapon, and Iran's revolution.

syria_line.title: The Golan Line, 1949–2026
syria_line.sub: From a declined peace offer to a fortification line inside Syria.

steps.x: Syria's new ruler offers peace and to resettle refugees; Ben-Gurion says no; an armistice with demilitarized zones follows.
Disputed zones and water; shelling and provocations on both sides; then the Golan is taken and its people displaced.
A disengagement agreement and a UN force — quiet for fifty years.
Israel extends its law; the Security Council rejects it; the 1990s talks come within a shoreline of a deal.
The US recognizes the annexation; Assad falls and Israel crosses the 1974 line.
Talks "90%" done by Syria's account; 500 strikes; the Sufa 53 line dug inside Syria.

turkey_arc.title: Turkey and Israel — From Ally to Rival
turkey_arc.sub: Four centuries of Ottoman rule, a quiet alliance, a raid, and a rivalry — with the oil that never stopped.

steps.x: Ottoman rule ends; the Sultan had refused Herzl; Turkey renounces the Arab provinces.
First Muslim-majority recognition, the Trident pact, the 1996 military agreements.
The Mavi Marmara raid ends the alliance.
Apology and compensation, expulsions, a 2022 thaw — then October 7 and a declared break.
Genocide warrants — while Azerbaijani oil keeps crossing Turkey — and a rivalry over Syria.

proxy_frame.title: The 'Proxy' Frame — Same Protocol, Different Origins
proxy_frame.sub: Iran backs all three. Each was born somewhere else — and Israel's own actions sit at the root of two.

steps.x: Hamas, Hezbollah and the Houthis presented as one Iranian "octopus."
Iran's documented money, arms and training for all three.

steps.t: What it leaves out — Lebanon and Palestine
steps.x: Hezbollah grew from Israel's 1982 invasion; Hamas from two decades of occupation.
The Houthis grew from a Yemeni revival, and their main war was with Saudi Arabia.
Paused during Gaza ceasefires; joined Iran's war in 2026.

uae_ledger.title: The UAE Ledger — Strong Ties, a Weak Promise
uae_ledger.sub: What the Abraham Accords locked in, and what they only promised.

steps.x: Israel and the UAE normalize; the US attaches a $23B arms package.
Trade and flights, arms in both directions, and Israeli spyware licensed by Israel's Defense Ministry.
Annexation paused in 2020 and pulled from the agenda after the 2025 red line.
Iran hits the UAE hardest; Israel puts an Iron Dome on Emirati soil.
A Palestinian state — the stated aim — remains undelivered.

oil_for_arms.title: Oil for Arms — Azerbaijan, Israel, and the Pipeline Across Turkey
oil_for_arms.sub: The documented swap, the route it travels, and who paid.

steps.x: Iran's northern neighbor and Israel — allies since the 1990s.
40–60% of Israel's crude, through Georgia to Turkey's Ceyhan, then by tanker.
About two-thirds of Azerbaijan's major weapons from Israel.
Two Karabakh wars; 100,000+ Armenians fled in a week in 2023.
A door to the US through Israel's friends — and a pipeline under Turkey's boycott.
